chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man praying in a single shirt, or in an unlined qabaʾ, or in a padded qabaʾ, while he is not wearing an izār. He said: “If the shirt is thick, and the qabaʾ is not long-slit, and the single garment is such that he wraps himself with it, and trousers are in that same position, all of that is unobjectionable. But when he wears trousers, he should place something over his shoulder, even if only a rope.”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: A free woman does not pray without a khimār upon her head, and that is permissible for female slaves and for young girls among free women.

key_terms.إِزَارٌ: a lower wrap or waist-garment not present in the case being asked about
key_terms.خِمَارٍ: a head covering required here for the free woman in prayer
key_terms.صَفِيقًا: thick or dense enough not to be too thin
key_terms.قَبَاءٍ: a cloak or outer garment discussed as valid prayer clothing
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt worn as a garment in prayer
key_terms.يَتَوَشَّحُ: to wrap oneself with a garment across the body
key_terms.ٱلسَّرَاوِيلَ: trousers, whose use in prayer is addressed here

ai.seo_question: What clothing is permissible for men and women to wear in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on what kinds of clothing are sufficient for salat (prayer), especially for a man praying in a single garment or in trousers. It also records that a free woman must pray with a head covering, while an allowance is mentioned for female slaves and young free girls.
